text:
alex_support: Heads-up — Customer ACME reported their monthly credits 'refilled' ~6 hours early for one subaccount. They saw tokens jump back to full and then drop to zero after a flurry of retries. Summary pasted from the customer below.

maria_billing: Which timezone is the tenant set to? Could be DST change or tenant tz mismatch.

alex_support: Tenant tz = America/Chicago. Customer says refill happened at 06:00 UTC instead of 00:00 CDT. They included screenshots.

ingrid_engineer: Can you drop the API request IDs + billing job logs? Might be duplicate job runs or a replay window. My hunch: refill job anchored in UTC while UI display is tenant-local -> visible mismatch.

alex_support: Req IDs: req_01FZ2A... and req_01GQ3B... Billing job log shows run at 06:00:12 UTC. Customer local midnight was 00:00 CDT (05:00 UTC). That looks like a 1-hour offset, not 6 — but customer reported '6 hours' maybe conflating local times.

sam_ops: Did the tenant recently toggle timezone or move regions? Check tenant metadata for `tz_changed_at`.

maria_billing: I checked — `tz_changed_at` = null. BUT billing job log indicates `billing_batch_window: "daily"` and `window_anchor: "00:00"` in UTC. We recently flipped a canary that pins batch runs to UTC for consistency.

ingrid_engineer: That would cause tenants expecting local-midnight refills to see an apparent early/late refill. Fix is to compute run_time = tenant_midnight_in_utc(tenant_tz) when scheduling per-tenant jobs. Also need a cache-bust so the UI doesn't show stale zero after refill.

alex_support: Customer asked for repro steps and a timeline. Suggested reply: explain the canary change, confirm we're rolling a fix, and offer a manual, one-off refill at their preferred local midnight as a temporary workaround.

sam_ops: Quick mitigation — I've started reverting the canary to tenant-aware scheduling on the canary ring. Rolling to 20% now. I'll watch for duplicate job runs and any surge in token counters.

ingrid_engineer: Found a secondary bug: UI display cache TTL was set to 10m which can keep a "0 credits" view even after backend refill. Plan: either lower TTL to 1s for credit keys or emit a cache-invalidate event after refill. Example repro commands below.

ingrid_engineer: Repro with mock tenant:
```
# set tenant tz
curl -X POST https://console.redwood.ai/admin/tenants/1234 -d '{"timezone":"America/Chicago"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer <admin-token>"
# simulate canary billing job run (UTC anchored)
./bin/billing_job --tenant 1234 --canary --run-at 2024-03-10T06:00:00Z
# observe display cache key
redis-cli GET ui:tenant:1234:credits
```

maria_billing: I'll draft the customer message: timeline, what happened, what we're doing, and offer the manual refill. Assign owners: sam_ops -> revert/monitor, ingrid_engineer -> cache invalidation + scheduling patch, maria_billing -> customer comms.

BILLING-BOT: Incident created INC-2024-4589, priority: P2. Assigned: sam_ops, ingrid_engineer, maria_billing.

alex_support: Thanks team — I'll message ACME with the interim workaround and link to INC-2024-4589. Will update here after they confirm. :thumbsup:
